Edtech unicorn PhysicsWallah (PW) appears to be changing its approach to student lending yet again. Its wholly owned subsidiary FinZ Finance has agreed to sell, transfer and assign a loan portfolio worth Rs 95.79 crore to RBI-registered NBFC Auxilo Finserve, as per the stock exchange disclosure.

The portfolio accounts for a substantial part of FinZ Finance’s total loan book, making the transaction significant for PW’s lending strategy.

The move comes after PhysicsWallah had positioned FinZ Finance as its in-house lending arm. The company had earlier said that FinZ would allow it to provide loans to students from its own books.

However, PW later shifted its approach and said it would work with third-party NBFCs to facilitate loans for its students instead of taking the entire lending exposure on its own balance sheet.

The change in strategy also comes against the backdrop of a mixed market response to PW’s earlier lending plans. Investors had raised questions around the capital requirements and risks associated with building an in-house lending business, when lending was not the company’s core business.

FinZ Finance received its NBFC licence in September 2025 and started operations in February 2026. A large portion of its lending was linked to PW’s student base.

PhysicsWallah reported a 24.4% year-on-year rise in revenue from operations to Rs 1,054 crore in Q1 FY27, while its net loss narrowed 30.7% to Rs 88 crore. The company’s online business grew 33.3% to Rs 549 crore, while offline revenue rose 14.5% to Rs 490 crore during the quarter.

Following the development, PhysicsWallah’s share price rose more than 6% on Monday. The stock was trading at Rs 128.1 as of 2:46 PM, giving the company a market capitalisation of around Rs 37,812 crore.

Manufacturing platform Zetwerk has filed its Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) for its initial public offering (IPO), comprising a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,830 crore.

According to its RHP, the Bengaluru-based company has increased its fresh issue size to Rs 2,830 crore from Rs 2,600 crore proposed in its updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP). The offer for sale (OFS) has also increased by 49% to 14.45 crore shares from 9.68 crore shares proposed in the UDRHP filed in August.

The OFS will include shares from promoters Amrit Pratik Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan, who will each sell 1.42 crore shares. Promoter group entity Creovate Innovation will offload up to 2.30 crore shares. Together, they will offer around 5.14 crore shares.

Among the existing investors, Lightspeed Venture Partners will offload the most, at 2.51 crore shares, followed by Peak XV Partners, which will sell 2.34 crore shares.

Kae Capital Fund and Kalysta Capital Fund will collectively sell up to 1.67 crore shares. Accel India V will also participate in the OFS, offloading up to 1.2 crore shares.

The offer will be open for subscription on October 15, 2026 to October 19, 2026 while anchor bid will start on October 14.

Zetwerk plans to use Rs 1,300 crore from the fresh issue to repay or prepay borrowings at the company level. Another Rs 860 crore will be used to repay debt at nine subsidiaries. The remaining proceeds will be allocated towards acquisitions, strategic investments and general corporate purposes.

Founded in 2017 by Acharya and Ramakkrushnan, Zetwerk operates a technology-led manufacturing platform that connects businesses with manufacturers and suppliers across sectors such as energy, electronics, aerospace, defence and industrial automation.

On the financial front, Zetwerk’s revenue from continuing operations rose to Rs 15,913 crore in FY26 from Rs 11,332 crore in FY25. In Q1 FY27, revenue from operations grew 55% year-on-year to Rs 4,118 crore, while losses from continuing operations declined 93% to Rs 64 crore from Rs 881 crore in the year-ago quarter.

A group of former Flipkart executives has launched a petition to get around 20,000-30,000 other former employees of the e-commerce platform and its group companies together to push for their inclusion in the planned $2 billion ESOPs buyback, as per an Economic Times report today.

The executives are looking to bring together ex-employees of ANS Commerce, Cleartrip, Flipkart , Myntra, Shopsy and Super Money together to push parent firm Walmart on their demands regarding the vested employee stock options ahead of the platform's IPO, it added.

The petition on 10 October comes days after executives emailed Walmart 's board seeking a buyout of their ESOPs. The report said that in response, the US-based company's legal counsel said former employees will be considered as part of liquidity in Flipkart's IPO, but did not specify commitments.

In the petition, the employees said that lack of clear timeline could leave them in limbo for years till the IPO comes to fruition. They added that this is a request for dialogue rather than legal notice or claim, the report added citing a source.

Bloomberg on 9 October reported that a group of former Flipkart executives urged Walmart to buy out their stock options, seeking to cash in while the US retailer weighs options including a separate listing for the India e-commerce operator.

With no visibility regarding the timing of the IPO, a group of eight former C-suite and senior executives said a purchase of their shares by Walmart would allow them to liquidate their holdings. The former executives appealed to Walmart’s board in a letter seen by Bloomberg News and earlier reported by the Economic Times, it said.

The ex-employees said they’ve held the stock options for as many as 15 years in some cases. Current Flipkart employees were offered the opportunity this year to sell stock options, the group said.

“We appreciate the perspective of all employees — current and former — and value their feedback. As with anything raised, we take it seriously,” Walmart told Bloomberg in a statement.

Flipkart was founded in Bangalore in 2007 by two former Amazon.com Inc. engineers, Sachin Bansal and Binny Bansal (who are not related). Just like Amazon, they began by selling books online before expanding to more expensive products such as electronics and smartphones, the report said.

In 2018, Walmart acquired a controlling stake in the company for $16 billion — its biggest-ever deal, bringing its high-stakes battle for online retail supremacy with Amazon to India. Sachin sold off his entire stake to Walmart and left. Binny too exited within months and sold off his remaining shares by 2023, it added.

Flipkart has said that its priority is to serve customers, and that an IPO is a target for the company. “An IPO remains an active part of our strategic roadmap, and we will move forward when the timing is right.
